title: D.B. Cooper — the only unsolved hijacking in US history
voiceover: On Thanksgiving Eve, 1971, a man calling himself Dan Cooper boarded a flight in Portland, Oregon. He was wearing a black suit. He ordered a bourbon and soda. He handed the flight attendant a note that said he had a bomb. He demanded 200 thousand dollars and four parachutes. He got them. Then somewhere over the forests of Washington state, he opened the back door of the plane and jumped out into a rainstorm. He has never been identified. His body has never been found. The money has never resurfaced. Fifty years later, the FBI has officially given up. D.B. Cooper is the only unsolved skyjacking in American history. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
